Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: Success Criteria, SDK Handoff & Tool-Calling Flow (Trial Plan)

Thanks again for the demo time today — appreciated the candid feedback. This thread captures the recommended success criteria and a proposed technical handoff for the 4-week trial so we can align owners and timelines quickly. High-level summary first, then owners & next steps.

Summary (key asks from Cortex):
- Validate hallucination rate on customer-facing summaries (target < 2% on our eval set)
- Confirm streaming latency for interactive flows (95th percentile < 250ms for 1-2 token bursts)
- Exercise tool-calling for the lookup & actions routes (auth + idempotency checks)

Proposed PoC success criteria (must be agreed by Friday 5/21):
1) Functional: Demo routes exercised end-to-end: /v1/generate (batch), /v1/stream (interactive), /v1/tools/run (tool-calls).
2) Quality: Passes the Cortex prompt-set regression (precision@top1 >= 0.88).
3) Performance: Sustained 50rps for batch test, 200 concurrent streaming sessions with 95p latency <250ms.
4) Reliability: Canary fallback to quantized variant when memory pressure is detected; no more than two failovers during the trial.

Technical handoff items (we'll attach the scope sheet):
- SDK: sample repo + routes.zip attached (sdk_sample_routes_v2.zip). Dev will use the Node SDK route examples; target on-ramp PR into your repo by week 1.
- Streaming: use /v1/stream with the RW-streaming protocol (chunked SSE). We'll provide a small client example that handles reconnection + resume of KV cache.
- Tool calling: tool-run must include idempotency_token header and attest flow (we'll show example body). Recommended: route the tool-call to /v1/tools/run and return 202 + job id when longer than 300ms.
- Caching: prefix KV cache enabled for the first 4 tokens of the prompt to reduce cold-starts; engineer-suggested TTL 15m for session caches.

Owners & immediate next steps:
- Jordan / Cortex: share a representative prompt set and a CSV of expected outputs (due 5/19).
- Dev (Dev Patel): prepare SDK samples + streaming client (deliver by 5/22).
- Marissa: commercial intake / trial SOW, overlay pricing + optional Dedicated quote (due 5/21).
- Tessa: CS onboarding checklist & support SLAs for trial (deliver by 5/20).

Attachments: poc_scope_v1.xlsx (high-level tasks & timeline), sdk_sample_routes_v2.zip (samples).

Ask: please confirm the criteria and owners inline and flag any adjustments. Once agreed I'll create the HubSpot milestone and a shared Drive folder.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Jordan — good questions, answering inline and adding tech notes.

Model & variants:
- For ~2k token context, recommended variant: rw-2k-qa-optimized (we'll pin this for the trial). It balances attention memory and latency; fallback to rw-quant-2k with 8-bit quantization if mem pressure occurs.

Tool-calling completion flow:
- Redwood supports webhook callbacks for job completions. We'll provide a signed callback with HMAC header for verification. Polling also supported but less efficient.
- Example: POST /callbacks/tool-complete with body { job_id, status, result_url } (we'll include sample signed header).

Logs & retention (trial):
- Default: token-level logs retained for 30 days for trial telemetry. Can shorten to 7 days for the PoC if Cortex needs tighter retention; note that reduces debugging capability for regressions.

SDK & streaming notes:
- SDK sample includes: authentication patterns, stream reconnection, resume with offset token and KV cache restore.
- Streaming backpressure: client should respect the RW-streaming retry-after header; we'll instrument the SDK to surface retry windows.

I'll attach a small example payload and the webhook spec to the Drive folder today.

Next steps (tech):
- Dev to push sdk_sample repo to shared Drive and open a small PR by 5/22.
- Dev + Jordan to do an integration sync Wed 5/20 (30 min) to walk streaming and tool-call flow.

-Dev
